soldier: Soldier: the head shape varies into two forms, elongate-oval and nearly circular. The elongate-oval form again occurs in two sizes, in the same colony the former making up about 70 per cent, the small elongate-oval form about 10 per cent and the nearly circular form about 20 per cent; nearly circular individuals differ only in having the broadest and largest head and a distinctly shorter postmentum, the remaining characters being very similar. Head, antennae and labrum yellow, mandibles reddish brown, pronotum pale yellow and paler in its posterior half, meso- and metathorax and abdominal tergites pale white. The sides of the fontanelle with two distinct bristles each, mostly one bristle between the antennal socket and the fontanelle, the head almost hairless, the disc with scattered short bristles, the hairs of the abdominal tergites rather long and rather dense. Mandibles rather straight, their tips only slightly curved; labrum longer than wide, slightly narrow in front; the fontanelle extending as a short tube, the aperture not visible in dorsal view, the fontanelle aperture nearly triangular. Antennae with 15 segments, the 3rd slightly short and small, or the 3rd and 4th almost equal. In the elongate-oval form the waist of the postmentum lies near the middle but towards the posterior, in the circular form the waist clearly at the posterior end. The anterior margin of the pronotum distinctly concave, the posterior margin indistinctly concave.
